description: The CoMSES Net Computational Model Library is a repository of agent-based and other computational models of social and ecological systems, each published with source code, narrative documentation such as ODD protocols, and structured metadata. At access it held 1,320 models, including many agricultural land-use, farm decision and food system models reachable through its land-use tag. It is run by CoMSES Net, the Network for Computational Modeling in Social and Ecological Sciences, supported by the US National Science Foundation and Arizona State University, with partners such as the Digital Research Alliance of Canada and DataCite. Coverage is global, as models describe places and systems worldwide. Browsing and downloading are free; models carry their own licences, users must cite the model authors, and a private peer review gives passing models a DOI. Caveats: quality and documentation vary between unreviewed models, and many are written for NetLogo or older software versions. For simulation it is a source of reusable agent-based models of farmers, land markets and supply chains that can be adapted to study how agricultural systems respond to droughts, floods or infrastructure failures. It is related to the MPMAS record in this catalogue, a farm agent-based model distributed outside the library.
